To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the present day relative abundances of sedimentary rocks are the result of the combined effect of sediment recycling and evolution.
(1) the present day thickness of the sedimentary rock pile is a consequence of recycling and (2) recycling has been a major factor in the evolution of sediments and sedimentary rocks.

the present day steady-state composition of the ocean is not a necessary condition for the secular trends in sedimentary rocks, that the secular changes in the composition of the ocean are a consequence of the secular variations in sediment composition, and that the secular trends in the composition of sedimentary rocks are the consequence of recycling and evolution of the ocean.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the sedimentary rocks.
the evolution of the sedimentary cycle and with the evolution of sediments as products of the sedimentary system.
the evolution of Earth’s sedimentary rocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

sedimentary rocks are the product of a complex interaction of the evolution of the Earth's surface, the evolution of the biosphere, the evolution of sedimentation and diagenesis, and the recycling of sediments.
recycling and evolution, as defined in this chapter, are complementary concepts.
recycling and evolution of the Earth are not only compatible but complementary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recycling is an important mechanism of the earth's surface processes and that it is a major factor in the evolution of sedimentation.
the evolution of the Earth's surface environment has been a continuous process of recycling, in which sedimentary rocks have played the central role.
recycling and evolution of sedimentary rocks are complementary and that both are important in understanding the evolution of the Earth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evolution of the sedimentary record can be understood in the context of a simple, uniformitarian model, provided that we take account of the effects of sediment recycling and of the evolution of life.
the evolution of the lithologic types of sedimentary rocks and of their geochemical composition are not independent.
the evolution of sediment is not a linear process.
